revision_history.description: Separated challenge pass over the safety-critical synthetic chain, performed after the domain reviews FB2-REV-000003..FB2-REV-000005 and FB2-REV-000007, and specifically aimed at false completeness, circular arguments, unsupported claims and metric gaming.

revision_history.description: Provenance repair by a separate session (opencode-2026-10-01-provenance-repair), not a re-review. All 16 reviewed_ids digests in this record were re-derived from the artefact files as they stand on disk in the correct profile (synthetic_reference).  16 of 16 named artefacts have been revised or had their bytes replaced since this review was issued, so this record is re-issued at revision 2 and its digest for those artefacts now names the current revision; per-artefact detail, including the superseded digest and the basis for each classification, is in digest_corrections.  The findings, dispositions, scope, checklist and reviewer_identity of the original pass are untouched by this repair. The digest refresh does not carry the weight of a re-review: the original reviewer session did not examine the current revision of the revised artefacts, and no substantive re-examination was performed here.

reviewer_identity.note: Automated review performed in a single AI coding-agent session (opencode). The model identifier is the identifier exposed to this session's runtime. No platform-issued session id was available to the reviewer, so session_id is a locally chosen label for this run and is not a platform-issued identifier. Per master-prompt clause 2.9 this is an automated review: it is NOT organizational independence, NOT human confirmation, and NOT a qualified-checker result. No human reviewer, independent party, or separate agent session participated.

scope: Full scope over the 21 synthetic_reference safety-critical artifacts named in reviewed_ids: the hazard analysis, the safety goal, FSR-000001..000004, the four safety analyses, the safety case, the TARA, the five security requirements and the three change records. This is the separated challenge pass required by master-prompt section 15 for safety-critical artifacts. Note that this pass was performed by the same automated session that produced the domain reviews; it is a separated pass in sequence and in checklist, and it is NOT an independent party. The reduced independence is stated in limitations[].

findings.description: Challenge-pass confirmation of the circular-argument risk in the safety chain. The safety case's ARG-004 claims the independent hardware monitor 'provides ASIL B parallel path for freedom from interference', citing FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 alone as evidence. But the freedom-from-interference argument is only as strong as the claim that the monitor is genuinely independent of the element it monitors, and that claim is asserted, not shown: FB2-SAF-ANL-000004 lists interference categories and mitigations by name, and FB2-SAF-ANL-000003 coupling category DFC-03 concedes that 'Main AFE path and independent monitor both connect to cell voltage tap' with the mitigation being 'separate tap points and separate harness', a design constraint rather than an analysis result. The safety case cites the conclusion (FSR-000004) and not the analysis that would have to establish it (ANL-000003 / ANL-000004). This is the circular shape the master prompt asks a challenge reviewer to look for: an argument that cites its own conclusion.
findings.evidence: FB2-SAF-SCS-000001 claims[0].arguments[3]: 'Independent HW monitor provides ASIL B parallel path for freedom from interference', evidence ['FB2-SAF-FSR-000004']. FB2-SAF-SAF-ANL-000003 coupling_categories[2] DFC-03 category 'shared_input' identifies the shared cell-voltage tap and states the mitigation as a design constraint in the HSI. Neither ANL-000003 nor ANL-000004 appears in the safety case's argument evidence.

findings.description: The safety goal FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 is assigned ASIL_D and the entire downstream chain inherits that classification, but the record carries no asil_justification. Every qualification argument in the corpus therefore rests on an ASIL_D assignment whose derivation is not recorded anywhere. This is a first-class missing input, not a formality: an ASIL classification determines the required rigor of everything downstream, so the corpus cannot show that it applied the right rigor even where it did apply it. This is also a standing medium-severity validator finding. The record asserts no ASPICE capability level and no certification, and this review asserts none either.
findings.evidence: FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 (both profiles): asil 'ASIL_D', asil_justification absent. corpus.py MUT-009 ASIL validator reports 'safety goal FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 ASIL ASIL_D lacks justification' twice, once per profile.

findings.description: None of the seven functional safety requirements carries a fault_reaction field, in either profile. The requirement schema does not require one, so this is not a schema violation, but it means the corpus has no machine-readable record of what the system is required to DO on detection of each fault: no reaction time, no reaction target, no degraded-mode statement per requirement. The fault reactions are recoverable from prose in the statements, and the analyses supply mechanism and reaction narratives, but the field is absent everywhere. Combined with the safety case's incorrect timing arithmetic (FB2-REV-FND-000131) this is how an incorrect timing claim survives: there is no structured reaction-time field for a checker to compare against. This is a standing medium-severity validator finding.
findings.evidence: Recursive presence check: 'fault_reaction' is absent from all 7 FSR records across both profiles. corpus.py MUT-008 completeness checker reports 'safety requirement FB2-SAF-FSR-00000N has no fault_reaction defined' 7 times, once per profile-qualified artifact.

findings.description: False-completeness challenge on the security chain: TARA-scoped search. The TARA and its five derived requirements were checked for the specific failure modes a challenge reviewer should look for - fabricated vulnerability data, asserted exploitability, certification or ISO/SAE 21434 conformance claims, and control-presence claims contradicted by source. None were found: the record declares is_iso_21434_tara=false, states 'No exploitability assessment of any kind was performed', cites no CVE, and every real_source_presence claim sampled was confirmed against the real source. Recorded as a clean result on a performed check.
findings.evidence: TARA method.is_iso_21434_tara false; method.limitations lists the absence of damage scenarios, attack-path analysis, attack tree, TARA review and residual-risk evaluation record; zero CVE-\d{4}-\d+ matches and zero CVSS matches in the record; all sampled file:line assertions matched.

dispositions.action: Accepted. The safety case argues freedom from interference by citing the requirement that asserts independence rather than the analyses that would have to demonstrate it. The analyses exist and are populated, so the fix is to cite them; that is an authoring change to the safety case, which this review did not make. Referred to the safety owner together with FB2-REV-FND-000131, which concerns the same record.

Accepted. An ASIL_D assignment without recorded justification is a genuine gap and cannot be honestly closed by this automated pass. No artifact was edited and no ASIL was changed. Carried forward as a standing finding.

Accepted. Adding a fault_reaction field is a schema and authoring change outside this review's write scope. The check that produced this finding is retained unchanged; it was not weakened and no requirement was relabelled to silence it.
No action required. Recorded as a verified-clean challenge criterion.

limitations: Automated AI review performed in a single agent session. It is not organizational independence, not human confirmation, and not a qualified-checker result (master-prompt clause 2.9).
human_approval_status is 'pending' for every artifact covered by this review. No human reviewer signed any of them.
No artifact covered by this review carries production authority or product verification credit.

This challenge pass was performed by the SAME automated session that produced the domain reviews FB2-REV-000003, FB2-REV-000004, FB2-REV-000005 and FB2-REV-000007. It is a separated pass in time and checklist and it re-derived its own checks rather than inheriting the domain reviews' conclusions, but it is NOT an independent reviewer, NOT organizational independence, and NOT a qualified challenge function (master-prompt clause 2.9 and section 15). A genuinely independent challenge would require a different reviewer.

Because independence is not achieved, a clean result in this record is weaker evidence than it would be from an independent challenger. The four findings above should be read as what an automated pass could find, not as the limit of what is wrong.

The challenge checklist covered: false completeness, circular arguments, unsupported numeric claims, fabricated vulnerability data, and approval or certification overclaim. It did NOT cover: WCET or schedulability analysis, quantitative fault-tree evaluation, ISO 26262 clause by clause adequacy, or hardware timing closure. None of these were performed.
The as_is profile's safety chain is not in this record's scope. It is challenge-reviewed separately by FB2-REV-000010.
No artifact in the covered set carries production authority, verification credit or human approval, and this review asserts no ASPICE capability level and no certification for any of them.
review_method: Adversarial re-reading of the safety chain with an explicit search for circular argument structure, unsupported numeric claims, missing machine-readable inputs that would let an incorrect claim survive, and fabricated or overclaimed data. Numeric claims were re-derived independently from the cited requirement statements.
